MRK.rationale: Merck's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe earnings collapse: net income of -$4.24B and EPS of -$1.72, driven by a $9B one-time Cidara charge and the pending Terns acquisition's ~$5.8B IPR&D charge. While revenue grew 4.9% YoY to $16.29B, the GAAP loss is not a one-off noise — it reflects aggressive M&A spending that will depress 2026 EPS to ~$4.35 (down 51.6% from $8.98 in 2025). The stock has rallied 48% from its 52-week low of $76.66 to $127.63, yet the P/E has ballooned to 35.3x — the top of its 365-day range (11.1–35.8) — while net margin has halved to 13.6% and ROE has fallen to 19.5% from 36.1% a year ago. This is the most expensive the stock has been on trailing earnings in the available window, precisely when fundamentals are at their weakest. The Keytruda patent cliff (late 2028) remains the dominant structural risk, with Keytruda accounting for ~49% of 2024 revenue. Gardasil sales declined 22% in Q1 due to China regulatory issues. The LITESPARK-012 readout failed. Q2 2026 EPS is expected to be $1.36, down 36.2% YoY. There is no near-term fundamental catalyst to justify the elevated multiple — the next earnings report (Aug 4) is more likely to be a de-rating event given the expected double-digit profit decline. The combination of deteriorating earnings trajectory, peak valuation, and concentrated Keytruda risk makes MRK strongly unattractive at current levels.
